cards.title: Asche zu Asche
cards.description: Rammstein's original 1997 Windows game, preserved for the browser: guide the figure through three cavern, concert and beach levels, shooting the floating band-member faces that open the way forward.
cards.instructions: Choose Load game in the Asche window and wait for the title screen — the first run downloads about 40 MB — then click the title screen to start. Hold Left/Right to move, Up to jump and Space to fire; Escape quits. On touch devices the game shows its own on-screen buttons. In level 3 the aggressive clone attacks while invisible: jump over it, then hold the opposite arrow briefly (~150 ms) to turn and fire — a quick tap can be missed by the game's keyboard polling, and jumping alone does not stop it. If the last life is lost, the wrapper shows a Game over overlay and restarts the game automatically after a short countdown; Play again now skips the wait.
cards.status: Playable — original 1997 game runs in the Asche browser emulator
cards.notes: The game is hosted separately at asche.rammwiki.mrzetti.com and embedded here with its compact click-to-load player; the desktop only frames it. Nothing downloads until Load game is chosen, closing the window releases the emulator, and the game page also offers a full-page link. Full death shows the original game-over screen; the wrapper then restarts the game automatically (or immediately with Play again now). The original email/fax high-score promotion has ended and is not restored. See the Asche project's RUNTIME.md and tools/ verification scripts for the emulator and game-file details.

cards.title: Mutter — Enhanced CD
cards.description: The data session of the US Mutter enhanced CD: a Universal Media Player shell for Windows 95 carrying the Sonne music video, album artwork, track data and 2001 web links, rebuilt here as a browser window.
cards.instructions: Use the toolbar in the preview. Media pages through the disc's artwork and plates; Video plays the Sonne music video (a labelled browser transcode); Audio lists the disc's eleven track entries; Connect shows the original web links; Help/Prefs shows the extracted manual and the player's credits. The original Windows program and the untranscoded MPEG-1 are downloads.
cards.status: Partial — data session preserved and previewed; the original Windows player is not run in the browser
cards.notes: The disc identifies itself in AUTORUN.INF as Mutter / Universal Records, selection 314549639-2, matching the US limited edition (Discogs release 614817, released 2 April 2001); that documented release supplies the year. The 41.4 MB Sonne.MPG is the original MPEG-1 video; the preview plays a documented H.264/AAC transcode. Universal Media Player 0.30 (Thinking Pictures Inc., © 1997) requires Windows 95 and QuickTime or Media Player for video and was not executed. The disc's audio tracks belong to the CD audio session and are not part of this data archive; its umusic.com/rock.com links are historical and not restored. Mutter.CDQ preserves album and track metadata alongside an embedded 'Enhanced CD' picture. See PROVENANCE.md and VERIFICATION.md.

Missing benzin1.flv, listpays.xml and historical score/form endpoints are not recreated. This site has no leaderboard backend. Archive label 2005 is not used as a verified year. cards.title: RAMMSTEIN Screensaver
cards.description: The 1999 Windows screensaver credited to Motor Music: red and green crosses and burning flames drift across a black screen while Rammstein lyric plates and the wordmark appear. Concept, design and programming: Guido Raschke; built with MacSourcery's CineMac engine and Macromedia Director 6.
cards.instructions: Open the preview for a browser animation rebuilt from the extracted original sprites (Pause/Resume and Next panel are available). The original is Windows-only and cannot run in a modern browser: download the extracted RST_saver.exe or the original installer for a compatible 32-bit Windows system or virtual machine. In the original, moving the pointer exits the screensaver; its credits screen reports version R2.2, 09.11.1999.
cards.status: Partial — Director 6 movie preserved and all sprites extracted; no browser Director runtime
cards.notes: RST_saver.exe is the 32-bit Director 6 MacroMix projector carved from the installer; its protected movie source_4.dir was rebuilt from the scattered chunk map and decompiled with ProjectorRays 0.2.1. All 103 8-bit BITD bitmaps were decoded with ScummVM's Director decoder and rendered with the movie's built-in system palette. The original has no sound. It requires Windows 95/98/NT4.0; the installer itself is a 16-bit NE program. See PROVENANCE.md and VERIFICATION.md for hashes and extraction evidence.
